review.headline: A very short Kennedy Variation game that ended too soon

sections.text: You answered 1.e4 with 1...e5 and White played 2.d4, the Center-style break. 2...Nc6?! was an inaccuracy that let White gain space. The engine preferred 2...exd4, trading in the centre.
3...d6?! was another small inaccuracy. 3...exd4 would have been best, as after 4.cxd4 d5 you would have had a good fight for the centre.
After 4.d5 the evaluation was only -0.5, so you were slightly worse and still had plenty of play. The game ended after just four moves, which looks like a premature resignation.

review.turning_point: Neither 2...Nc6?! nor 3...d6?! was a disaster, but together they let White play 4.d5 and gain space for free.
review.focus: At move 2, 2...exd4 would have resolved the centre. When a pawn is attacked in the centre, trade it before developing the knight.
